title: Volume 1 Chapter 11: Sortie
content: Chapter 11: Sortie
“Honestly, doing whatever you want!”
Dr. Allison poked her head through the open hatch of the cockpit, venting her frustration at me for deciding to deploy.
“You knew full well that the preparations weren’t complete enough to launch, didn’t you? So what were you thinking?”
Though she was complaining, Dr. Allison held a tablet in her hand and was multitasking.
“…The machine and systems are all green.”
After finishing her checks, Dr. Allison let out a small sigh and ended her scolding.
Feeling guilty for my selfish actions, I apologized sincerely.
“I truly apologize for this incident.”
“Yes, it’s really troublesome,” Dr. Allison stated firmly, apparently deciding there was no need to hold back with me.
As I regretted having betrayed their expectations, Dr. Allison gave me a mischievous smile.
“You’ll repay the trouble with data, won’t you? …Just now, your magic power output surged sharply. It’s currently holding steady at thirty percent.”
“Really!?”
I looked up in surprise, and Dr. Allison nodded as she showed me the screen on her tablet.

“Dr. Smith is making a big fuss about it. This gives us a little hope. With the force field defense, the data suggests you shouldn’t fall behind a Second Class. It’s a pleasant surprise, but it seems the force field also affects buoyancy. We might be able to save on fuel and propellant as well. The only downside is there’s little power left to allocate to weaponry.”
Along with the increase in magic power output, the total weight of Thunderbolt decreased.
Dr. Smith and Dr. Allison concluded it was due to the force field effect, but since it remains unexplained, further investigation is necessary.
Though I haven’t secured full magic power, thirty percent output is enough for movement and defense.
“Is it still insufficient for weapon use?”

“To be honest, the buoyancy and force field defense are also lacking. Don’t forget, this is barely performance enough to deploy in actual combat. No matter how powerful the weapons are, they’re just distractions against Gijuu. Focus on supporting your buddy.”
I was firmly told to quietly dedicate myself to supporting Louise, and I nodded silently after hearing Dr. Allison’s explanation.
“Understood.”
After hearing my reply, Dr. Allison gave a slight smile before tightening her expression.
“I’m closing the hatch. Prepare for sortie! All personnel, clear away from the machine!”
As Dr. Allison spoke, the hatch of Thunderbolt slowly closed.
Once sealed tightly and locked, outside sounds faded away.
The cockpit grew even darker, with the glow of monitors and instruments becoming clearly visible.
There were two large monitors stacked vertically in front of me, and one on each side.
I heard the field of view was wider than with the naked eye.
A rear monitor was also installed.
To fully activate the machine, I pressed switches and toggled settings.
The operators were Dr. Smith and Dr. Allison.
“Ahhh! Our experimental machine is finally being deployed in combat, Allison-kun!”
“Dr. Smith, please sit quietly! …Thunderbolt, we confirm full activation here. Personnel evacuation confirmed. Raise the machine to the designated position.”
“I’m raising the machine.”
When I spoke for confirmation, my voice echoed outside through the external speakers.
The Thunderbolt, which had been lying down in the transport aircraft’s hangar, was slowly raised upright by fixed fixtures.
Once it reached a standing posture, I heard the voices of the workers.
“Unlocking fixture locks.”
The devices holding it in place detached, and Thunderbolt stood on its two legs inside the hangar.
“Converting magic power output to buoyancy… weight reduction confirmed.”
“Unlocking large rifle lock. Thunderbolt, please manually equip the large rifle.”
I took the large rifle prepared on the hangar wall in my right hand.
The manipulator—an essential feature of humanoid weapons—grasped the grip of the large rifle.
“Thunderbolt, sortie preparation complete. Ready for deployment at any time.”
Before I knew it, the fixtures were stored away in the wall, leaving only Thunderbolt standing.
The signal light on the ceiling, indicating readiness for sortie, changed from red to yellow, then to blue.
“Ignition.”
The jet engines installed on Thunderbolt started up, and the machine, lightened by magic power, began to lift.
However, wires attached to the back prevented Thunderbolt from taking off.
This wasn’t a forgotten fixture but a device to build momentum.
As the jet engines increased thrust, a roaring sound reverberated throughout the hangar, and the temperature rose rapidly.
…It’s about time.
“Everyone, brace for shock!”
The workers exiting the hangar prepared for the vibrations caused by the sortie.
The wires snapped from the strain, and with that momentum, Thunderbolt shot out from the transport aircraft.
“Ugh!”
The pressure from ahead pushed my body into the cockpit seat.
Though I had conducted many flight tests, launching from a transport aircraft was only something I had experienced in manuals and simulators, so I was relieved it succeeded.
“…Louise came too.”
Louise noticed me as I shot out from the transport aircraft and approached.
[img]https://i.imgur.com/0vk01yj.jpeg
Since the humanoid weapon, including its armaments, exceeded six meters in length, the Valkyrie’s Battle Dress looked small in comparison.
The structure of the Valkyrie’s Battle Dress exposed much of the body.
From my perspective, protected by the humanoid weapon, her appearance was somewhat worrying.
However, Louise didn’t seem to feel the wind pressure or heaviness even at Mach speeds.
“That’s the rumored experimental machine? It’s my first time seeing it, but it’s huge.”
Watching Louise casually talk while flying, I was reminded how extraordinary Valkyries really were.
“This experimental machine is particularly large even among its kind.”
“Ohh, I see.”
Louise flew around Thunderbolt like an acrobat, inspecting the machine.
She looked like a fairy from a fairy tale.
As we neared the destination, Louise’s somewhat absent-minded demeanor vanished.
She stopped watching Thunderbolt and prepared her weapons for immediate use.
“…Yeah, we’re almost there. Lifting restrictions on all weapons.”
With the leader Louise’s decision, weapon use was authorized and safeties disengaged.
“Ren-kun, I’ll support you from here, but if it gets too bad, retreat. Above all, prioritize your own life.”
“R-Right…”
Before I could finish my reply, I shifted my gaze to the sea surface.
I saw what appeared to be Third Class Gijuu heading toward the shore to land.
“Third Class!?”
Instinctively, I raised my weapon and took aim, but Louise stopped me.
“What are you doing!? Don’t engage the Third Class!”
“But, still—!?”
The instincts ingrained from my infantry days strongly urged me to attack the massive group of Third Class Gijuu heading for the beach.
I intuitively understood that if even a few reached the shore, the infantry units would suffer casualties.
I had checked the infantry deployment and numbers before sortie, so it was naturally in my mind.
And now, I had the equipment to easily slaughter Third Class enemies.
My desire to help my comrades—the infantry—narrowed my vision.
I knew it was wrong in my head.
But my heart wouldn’t accept it.
I felt frustrated that I had the power to save even one infantry soldier from the brutal ground battles, yet the environment forbade it.
Louise warned again to ignore the Third Class.
“We don’t have the luxury to waste ammo on Third Class right now! Especially since your machine doesn’t have a Subspace Container!”
The Subspace Container—that was one of the advantages Valkyries had over fighter jets.
Valkyries had personal spaces in subspace where they stored weapons and ammunition.
They could use weapons and ammo without worrying about load, giving them excellent endurance.
Thunderbolt was loaded with as many weapons as possible, but it lacked any function to store ammo in subspace.
Even fully loaded like an armory, it couldn’t match the Valkyries in armament.
Yes, it couldn’t match them—but still—
“—Understood. Louise, I’m sorry.”
When I obediently backed down, Louise sighed in relief.
“No, I understand how you feel, Ren-kun, but right now rescuing our comrades is the top priority. Look, they’re almost close enough to see with the naked eye.”
On the monitor, I could see something the size of a grain of sand.
When the image zoomed in, it showed Valkyrie candidates surrounded by Gijuu, fleeing in panic.
Their ammo was already depleted, weapons broken, barely able to resist.
But they were alive.
“They’re alive! Louise, they’re still alive!”
Just as I thought we made it in time, Louise moved.
Her Battle Dress was armed with a large rifle with a long barrel designed for mid-to-long range.
Mounted on her large sub-arm was some kind of optical weapon.
Louise raised her rifle and quickly pulled the trigger.
Once, twice… Even at this considerable distance, Louise’s shots pierced the Gijuu attacking our allies.
I was amazed at Louise’s marksmanship.
She was definitely better than Shy Boy, and on top of that, she had the courage and composure.
“…At this distance, it lacks a decisive blow. I’ll close in. Ren-kun, my weapons aren’t suited for close combat, so please handle any Gijuu that come near.”
“Understood!”
Louise’s bullets pierced the Gijuu but didn’t destroy them.
Apparently, range was an issue, so we both closed the distance.
The enemies noticed our arrival and had already taken action.
Some of the Second Class Gijuu surrounding our allies flew toward us.
I aimed the Gatling gun on Thunderbolt’s left arm and pulled the trigger on the control stick.
The barrels spun, firing bullet after bullet, vibrations reaching the cockpit.
I understood the weapon prioritized power, but continuous fire destabilized the machine’s posture, which was a problem.
“For Gijuu, a smaller caliber might be easier to handle.”
While muttering this, bullets kept hitting the advancing Second Class.
However, the force fields protecting the Second Class Gijuu rendered the attacks ineffective.
I could see the bullets scraping the surface beyond the force field, but they lacked the power to pierce the beasts’ bodies.
They only managed to scratch the outer shell.
The power drop was likely caused by the bullets hitting the force field.
“Lack of magic power.”
It was clear that the magic power supplied to the weapons was insufficient.
Still, it seemed to serve well enough as a delay tactic.
Louise mercilessly shot the slightly damaged Second Class Gijuu, whose flight speed had dropped.
When the live rounds blew off a Gijuu’s head, it fell into the sea, still flying for a while due to momentum.
Louise called out to our allies.
“I’m here to help. Hurry and break through the encirclement!”
While firing, she tried to secure a retreat route for our allies, but Lieutenant Asai, the First Squad leader, wore a bitter expression.
“Kanako was hit and can’t fly well! She charged recklessly to secure our retreat and drew concentrated fire!”
Lieutenant Nishitani, held by Lieutenant Asai, seemed unconscious.
Fortunately, she was still alive, but surrounded by enemies, there was a high risk both would be shot down together.
Lieutenant Suzuki’s brave expression before sortie was gone.
“We’re out of weapons and ammo! They keep sending reinforcements! What are the Boots Cat guys doing...?”
Out of ammo, weapons broken and unusable.
They were pushed into a desperate situation, mentally cornered.
Still, even while complaining, she tried to protect Lieutenant Nishitani, which was admirable.
Louise’s expression grew grim.
“—At least save the two of them.”
She seemed to be considering abandoning Nishitani and rescuing only Lieutenants Asai and Suzuki.
It was certainly rational and the right decision for this situation.
But I felt a strong discomfort at the method Louise seemed to choose.
Louise sniped from a distance, but the enemy numbers were too many to handle.
The First Squad was running, but carrying the immobile Nishitani meant they couldn’t escape quickly.
Gradually, the Gijuu’ attacks wore down the force fields protecting them.
At this rate, all three would be shot down soon.
Seeing Asai and Suzuki shielding Nishitani reminded me of that day’s scene.
The day the humanoid Gijuu attacked and my squad was wiped out, leaving me behind.
That one-sided massacre had been deeply etched into my heart.
“…No good.”
“Ren-kun, what’s wrong? Even if it’s ineffective, provide cover—”
“No. I won’t let it happen. I won’t let it happen!!”
I pressed the foot pedal to the limit, and Thunderbolt’s jet engines accelerated sharply.
The pressure pinned me to the seat, but I ignored it, focusing only on how to fix this situation.
“I’ll be the decoy! First Squad, retreat while you can!”
Thunderbolt plunged into the Gijuu swarm, opening the missile container hatches on its legs and firing small missiles.
Eighteen small missiles shot out from all four legs, attacking the Gijuu.
Though small, the missiles had tracking functions and hit even Gijuu attempting evasive maneuvers, causing explosions.
Explosions erupted all around, engulfing the Gijuu in flames.
However, due to insufficient magic power, the damage was minimal.
They only scorched the surface of the Gijuu.
At best, it was just enough to delay and distract.
Still, I flew around within the Gijuu swarm.
I jettisoned the empty missile containers to lighten the machine, then heard Louise’s voice.
“What are you doing!? Return, Ren-kun!”
“I’ll handle this alone! Louise, escort First Squad and fall back!”
The Gijuu targeted Thunderbolt.
From the gaps in their outer shells, multiple glowing orbs fired beam-like attacks.
I once thought these were optical weapons, but from what I learned in academy classes, they were “attacks reproduced by magic power.”
They weren’t as fast as optical weapons, nor true beams.
In academy terms, they were magic.
“Ugh!”
I dodged the beam-like attacks while flying around.
“Haha! When I saw them on the ground, I didn’t even have time to run, but riding this makes it easy to avoid!”
My tone grew rough with excitement.
Seeing me succeed in drawing the Gijuu’ attention, Louise acted as expected, making a rational decision.
“I’ll definitely come back! Stay safe until then, Ren-kun!”
Seeing her almost on the verge of tears wishing for my safety, I relaxed my mouth into a smile.
“…Understood.”
